question: Examine whether $f(x)=x-\ln x$ is strictly increasing on $(1,\infty)$. Justify your answer using the first derivative.
explanation:
Domain under consideration
The function is examined only for $x>1$, where $\ln x$ is defined.
First derivative
$$f'(x)=1-\frac{1}{x}=\frac{x-1}{x}$$
Sign of numerator and denominator
For $x>1$, both $x-1>0$ and $x>0$. Therefore,
$$\frac{x-1}{x}>0$$
Monotonicity criterion
Since $f'(x)>0$ at every point of $(1,\infty)$, the function increases as $x$ increases throughout this interval.
Conclusion
Hence, $f(x)=x-\ln x$ is strictly increasing on $(1,\infty)$.
